title: Transmission Media
markdown:
A **transmission medium** is anything that can carry information from a source to a destination. It is the physical path between a sender and a receiver in a data-communication system.

The transmission medium lies beneath the **Physical Layer** of the OSI model and is directly controlled by it — including the type of signal, the bit encoding, and the transmission rate.

{{viz:0}}

### Classification

Transmission media fall into two broad categories:

- **Guided (Wired) Media** — Signals are directed along a physical conductor such as a cable. Examples include twisted-pair cable, coaxial cable, and fiber-optic cable.
- **Unguided (Wireless) Media** — Signals propagate through free space without a physical conductor. Examples include radio waves, microwaves, and infrared.
